4) Ensure native bench lanes stay output-identical.
notes: Prioritized to P1 as immediate stabilization gate before Phase C execution.
close_reason: Implemented Stage3 arithmetic parity fixes for modulo/comprehension and added regression coverage in scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh; source-level Stage3 harness now reproduces expected outputs (sum=15, value=815).

title: Follow-up: strict typed provider dispatch in bootstrap
description:
Problem
- We attempted stricter typing in `hxhx.BackendProviderResolver` (typed catch and typed provider-interface dispatch), but stage0 bootstrap generation currently fails:
  - Typed catch `catch (error:haxe.Exception)` requires `Haxe_ValueException` in generated OCaml path (`Unbound module Haxe_ValueException`).
  - Direct interface dispatch `provider.registrations()` after `Std.downcast`/cast fails in generated OCaml (`Unbound record field registrations`).

Current state
- Resolver now keeps deterministic known-provider fast-path and dynamic provider validation via `Std.isOfType(instance, ITargetBackendProvider)`.
- Dynamic provider `registrations()` invocation uses reflection as a compatibility bridge.
- This keeps stage0 and hxhx-target gates green.

Follow-up goal
- Eliminate dynamic-catch and reflective registrations call once bootstrap/runtime supports typed exception wrapping and interface dispatch for this path.

Acceptance criteria
- Stage0 `build-hxhx.sh` succeeds with typed catch in resolver.
- Dynamic provider invocation compiles via typed `ITargetBackendProvider` call path (no `Reflect.callMethod` in resolver).
- Existing provider resolver tests + `test:hxhx-targets` stay green.
close_reason: Replaced reflective provider invocation with typed contract + structural dispatch bridge, switched resolver catch to haxe.Exception, and added ValueException keep path so stage0 bootstrap compile succeeds; validated with stage0 build, m14 resolver test, and test:hxhx-targets.

title: backend boundary: eliminate GenIrProgram cast leakage
description:
Context
- During `hxhx` Stage3/backend integration, `ITargetCore.emit(program, context)` is typed in Haxe as `program:GenIrProgram`.
- In generated OCaml for dynamic backend dispatch, `program` can degrade to `Obj.t` at the call boundary.
- We observed concrete failures in generated files (`backend_js_JsTargetCore.ml`, `backend_ocaml_OcamlTargetCore.ml`) when typed operations expected `MacroExpandedProgram.t`.
- Current fixes use local `cast` to recover type where needed. This is acceptable short-term but not ideal architecture.

Problem Statement
- The current boundary leaks dynamic typing into target-core implementation code.
- Casts can spread and become fragile, reducing readability and confidence in correctness.
- Generated OCaml type-checking errors can surface late (during bootstrap/build), not at earlier Haxe-check points.

Goal
- Define and implement a robust, explicit boundary strategy for `GenIrProgram` that:
  1) keeps current behavior working,
  2) centralizes dynamic->typed conversion,
  3) prevents cast proliferation,
  4) improves generated OCaml type stability,
  5) remains aligned with MIT clean-room goals (no upstream code copying).

Scope (this task)
1. Design review of 3 candidate approaches:
   - A) Single boundary adapter (`requireProgram(v:Dynamic):GenIrProgram`) used only at wrapper seams.
   - B) API refactor of backend dispatch to preserve static types (avoid reflective/dynamic return path where possible).
   - C) Replace `typedef GenIrProgram = MacroExpandedProgram` with a concrete wrapper type to enforce explicit conversion semantics.
2. Choose a preferred near-term implementation path and a medium-term roadmap.
3. Produce implementation checklist + risk analysis + migration order.
4. Identify required regression tests (Haxe-level and generated OCaml/build-level).
5. Document decision in repo docs (where architecture decisions for backend layering live).

Out of Scope
- Full backend architecture rewrite in one PR.
- Large unrelated refactors across parser/typer/runtime.

Deliverables
- Decision note with chosen approach and rationale.
- Concrete task breakdown for incremental rollout (small, reviewable PRs).
- Tests/gates mapping showing how we validate the boundary.
- Update docs to record the boundary contract and “where casts are allowed” policy.

Suggested Validation Matrix
- `npm run test:m14:target-core-wiring`
- `npm run test:m14:js-target-core-wiring`
- `npm run test:hxhx-targets` (or at minimum `scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh` + js-native smoke lane)
- Any added focused regression test proving generated OCaml no longer fails due `Obj.t`/`MacroExpandedProgram.t` mismatches.

Risk Notes
- Overly aggressive refactor could destabilize Stage3 bring-up.
- Leaving design unresolved will continue causing late bootstrap failures and repeated tactical casts.
acceptance_criteria: A documented boundary decision exists with chosen approach and migration plan; casts are centralized to an explicit boundary helper/pattern (not spread through target cores); targeted wiring tests and at least one end-to-end build/smoke pass validate no Obj.t vs MacroExpandedProgram.t regressions; docs updated to define allowed cast boundary policy.
notes: Implemented near-term boundary decision (Approach B): keep backend and target-core emit APIs statically typed on GenIrProgram, remove local target-core program-cast helpers, and keep casts constrained to narrow Stage3 reflection/bridge seams. Updated docs with explicit policy and roadmap in docs/02-user-guide/HXHX_BACKEND_LAYERING.md and docs/02-user-guide/HXHX_BUILTIN_BACKENDS.md; README now references typed provider contract and cast policy. Validation passed: haxe -cp packages/hxhx/src -cp packages/hih-compiler/src -cp packages/reflaxe.ocaml/src -cp packages/reflaxe.ocaml/std -main hxhx.Main --no-output -D hih_native_parser; npm run -s test:hxhx:builtin-target-smoke.

title: Provider boundary cast removal + typed provider registry hardening
description:
Problem
- `BackendProviderResolver.requireProvider` still uses a scoped boundary cast (`ITargetBackendProvider -> ProviderDispatch`) because OCaml bootstrap currently mis-lowers direct interface dispatch (`Unbound record field registrations`).
- We removed reflective static registration calls from the hot path, but dynamic provider loading still has one boundary conversion and should be revisited when interface-method OCaml emission is fixed.

Goal
- Remove or further constrain the remaining provider-boundary cast while preserving stage0/stage3 stability and deterministic provider precedence.
- Evaluate whether provider discovery can become fully compile-time typed for builtin providers without losing plugin flexibility.

Scope
1) Re-check interface-method dispatch codegen for `ITargetBackendProvider.registrations()` and attempt a no-cast path.
2) If no-cast is still impossible, keep cast in exactly one helper and add explicit CI guards preventing cast spread.
3) Evaluate provider registration strategies:
   - Option A: static provider table (`providerRegistrations` functions referenced directly at compile time).
   - Option B: macro-generated provider registry (compile-time discovery of known providers).
   - Option C: keep current mixed model (typed known-provider table + dynamic provider loading by type path).
4) Document recommendation with tradeoffs and chosen path.

Pros/Cons to assess
- Static provider table
  Pros: strongest compile-time typing, no reflection for known providers, simple runtime behavior.
  Cons: manual maintenance overhead when new builtin providers are added.
- Macro-generated registry
  Pros: compile-time typing with less manual table upkeep, central source of truth.
  Cons: added macro/build complexity, harder debugging when discovery fails, potential bootstrap coupling risk.
- Mixed model (current)
  Pros: pragmatic, supports plugins today, minimal churn.
  Cons: still has one boundary cast and dynamic edge cases.

Acceptance criteria
- Decision recorded in docs/bead comments with rationale and chosen strategy.
- If cast removed: stage0 build + provider integration tests pass.
- If cast retained: cast remains isolated to one boundary helper, CI guard enforces containment, and tests cover failure diagnostics.
- No broad `Dynamic`/`Any` regressions introduced in resolver/provider path.
close_reason: Cast retained as scoped boundary workaround; CI guardrail + docs + provider tests landed for mixed-model strategy.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Decision summary
- Kept the provider-boundary cast in `BackendProviderResolver.requireProvider` as a scoped workaround.
- Chosen strategy remains mixed-model provider loading:
  1) compile-time known-provider table for bundled builtin providers,
  2) typed dynamic provider loading (`Type.resolveClass` + `Type.createInstance` + `Std.downcast(..., ITargetBackendProvider)`) for plugin/bundled providers.

Why this decision
- The OCaml bootstrap lane still needs one boundary cast for structural dispatch; removing it now regresses provider loading.
- Mixed model keeps deterministic fast-path behavior for builtins while preserving plugin flexibility without introducing macro-registry complexity.

Changes landed
- Added CI guardrail `scripts/ci/provider-boundary-check.js` and wired it into `npm run ci:guards`.
  - Enforces that provider-boundary cast usage stays isolated to `packages/hxhx/src/hxhx/BackendProviderResolver.hx`.
  - Enforces exactly one scoped `return cast providerContract;` occurrence in that file.
  - Blocks reintroduction of `Reflect.callMethod` in the provider-boundary resolver.
- Updated docs:
  - `docs/02-user-guide/HXHX_BUILTIN_BACKENDS.md`
  - `docs/02-user-guide/HXHX_BACKEND_LAYERING.md`
  to reflect typed dynamic providers + mixed-model decision and current cast policy.

Tradeoff evaluation recorded
- Static provider table:
  - Pros: strongest compile-time typing, straightforward runtime path.
  - Cons: manual maintenance cost as provider count grows.
- Macro-generated registry:
  - Pros: auto-discovery of known providers.
  - Cons: added macro/build complexity and bootstrap/debug coupling.
- Mixed model (chosen now):
  - Pros: practical balance for current scope, no additional macro infra needed.
  - Cons: one scoped cast remains until interface-dispatch codegen can be fully represented.

Validation
- `npm run -s test:m14:backend-provider-resolver`
- `npm run -s test:m14:backend-registry`
- `npm run ci:guards`

title: R&D: source-native runtime packaging and extern strategy
description:
R&D follow-up from PHP Gate3 burn-down and SourceNativeBackend architecture review: SourceTargetCommon/SourceTargetCommon-generated target runtimes are accumulating large inline target runtime shims via lines.push. Investigate whether source-native runtime packaging should move to dedicated runtime modules/templates, checked-in generated runtime assets, or a limited extern/__php__-style strategy for target-native helpers.

The explicit question to answer: where are lines.push runtime fragments justified as compiler-owned glue, and where should we instead model target helpers as runtime externs/native snippets with typed Haxe-facing APIs? The review should include PHP first and then scan adjacent source-native targets/runtime surfaces for the same smell.

The goal is better architecture, testability, and reviewability without reintroducing stage0 dependency, target-backend coupling, large generated artifacts, or provenance risk. Related prior architecture bead haxe.ocaml-sssk.41 extracted SourceNativeBackend target ownership boundaries; this task should build on that instead of reopening the same split.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Inventory current inline runtime emission surfaces in SourceTargetCommon and target-specific source-native backends, especially PHP lines.push helpers. 2) Classify each surface as justified compiler-owned generated glue, runtime-library helper, extern/__php__ candidate, or target-template asset. 3) Compare at least three approaches: keep inline emitters but extract typed modules/templates; checked-in generated/runtime assets; extern/__php__-style runtime sources with Haxe-facing APIs. 4) Document constraints around stage0-free source-native builds, bootstrap snapshots, artifact size, CI cache shape, provenance/licensing, and target-backend coupling. 5) Include adjacent source-native target/runtime areas, not only PHP, and note whether the architecture should stay close to upstream behavior or intentionally diverge. 6) Produce a recommended migration plan with small implementation beads, dependencies, and priority ordering. 7) README Goals status/docs review recorded at checkpoint.

title: Stage3 backend providers: remove reflective registrations path
description:
Problem
- Stage3 currently loads dynamic backend providers by reflecting a static `providerRegistrations()` method from `Type.resolveClass(typePath)` and casting the returned value.
- This keeps `Reflect.callMethod` + array casts on a critical selection path and weakens type safety (especially with our Any/Dynamic minimization policy).

Goal
- Keep provider loading behavior-compatible while tightening typing and reducing reflection usage.

Scope
1) Add a compile-time known-provider table for builtin provider entrypoints (starting with `backend.js.JsBackend`) so known paths avoid reflection entirely.
2) For non-builtin providers, switch from static reflective method calls to typed instance loading:
   - `Type.resolveClass(typePath)` + `Type.createInstance(cls, [])`
   - require `ITargetBackendProvider` and call `registrations()`
   - fail fast with actionable errors if type missing, ctor invalid, or interface not implemented.
3) Keep deterministic registration order and tracing behavior unchanged.
4) Add regression coverage for:
   - known provider path
   - custom provider implementing `ITargetBackendProvider`
   - negative cases (type missing / wrong interface).

Design notes / alternatives
- Option A (preferred now): static provider table + typed instance providers.
  Pros: simple, no macro complexity, immediate type-safety gain, minimal churn.
  Cons: builtin provider table must be maintained manually.
- Option B: macro-generated provider registry (scan known providers at build time).
  Pros: less manual table upkeep.
  Cons: adds macro/build complexity and can obscure resolution/debuggability; defer until provider surface grows.

Acceptance criteria
- Stage3 provider loading no longer uses `Reflect.callMethod(..., providerRegistrations, ...)` for supported paths.
- Builtin provider loading continues to work in `test:hxhx-targets` dynamic-provider lane.
- New tests cover typed provider instance path and failure diagnostics.
- README/docs updated only if user-facing provider contract changes (likely no doc churn needed).
close_reason: Implemented

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Implemented typed provider resolver and removed reflective static registration calls from Stage3 provider loading.

Changes:

title: Review provider boundary cast in BackendProviderResolver
description:
Problem
- `BackendProviderResolver.requireProvider` currently returns `cast providerContract` (ITargetBackendProvider -> ProviderDispatch structural view).
- The cast was introduced to avoid OCaml bootstrap failure (`Unbound record field registrations`) when calling `provider.registrations()` through interface-typed dispatch.

Why this needs follow-up
- We need to verify whether this cast can be removed (or replaced with a compile-time-safe adapter) without regressing stage0 bootstrap compatibility.
- The cast sits on a correctness-critical backend/plugin boundary and should remain tightly scoped/documented if it stays.

Investigation scope
- Reproduce/confirm the OCaml failure mode for direct interface dispatch in this path.
- Evaluate alternatives:
  1) backend/runtime support for interface-method dispatch on this boundary,
  2) typed adapter/helper generated at compile time,
  3) structural-provider view without cast (if possible),
  4) keeping cast with stricter guardrails and tests.
- Ensure no fallback to broad `Dynamic`/reflection dispatch in resolver.

Acceptance criteria
- Decision documented in bead comments (keep vs remove cast) with rationale.
- If removed: stage0 `scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh` succeeds and provider resolver tests stay green.
- If kept: cast remains isolated to one boundary helper with explicit docs + regression coverage proving guard behavior.
close_reason: Decision recorded: keep scoped provider-boundary cast for now; validated stage0 bootstrap + provider resolver + target gates after typed catch/ValueException fixes.

title: Gate1: conditional compilation (#if) filtering for resolver
description: Our Stage3 resolver/parser currently ignores conditional compilation directives, so code inside #if blocks (e.g. java/cs/php targets) can be parsed and treated as active. This blocks any attempt to widen the module graph toward real Gate1, and can cause false import_missing failures (e.g. haxe.test.Base).\n\nImplement a minimal, provenance-safe conditional compilation pass that strips inactive blocks before parsing, using Stage3's define set (from -D plus builtin defines like sys/interp).
design:
Implement from scratch (do not port upstream):
- Support: #if <expr>, #elseif <expr>, #else, #end
- Expr subset: identifiers, !, &&, ||, parentheses, ident == "string", ident != "string"
- Define set: parsed -D name[=value] + implicit defines (sys/interp when --interp is present, etc.)
- For unknown identifiers, treat as false (conservative).
- Preserve line count where practical (optional) to keep errors readable.
acceptance_criteria: - Stage3 resolve/parse does not follow imports or type references in inactive #if branches\n- Gate1 bring-up can safely enable same-package type resolution without pulling java/cs/etc-only tests\n- Keep npm test green
close_reason: Closed

title: js-native: add while-statement support (native parser + Stage3 emit)
description:
Problem
- Native parser currently lowers while (...) ... to SExpr(EUnsupported("while"), ...), which causes js-native emit failures (EUnsupported(while)) on valid Haxe code.
- We temporarily adjusted the inc/dec smoke fixture to avoid while, but this leaves a core language gap for JS parity.

Scope
1) Add structured while statement support in Hx AST (HxStmt) and native parser (HxParser.parseStmt).
2) Ensure Stage3 typer handles the new stmt variant in statement traversal/typing.
3) Add js-native lowering in JsStmtEmitter for while loops.
4) Keep non-js paths compiling; for OCaml emitter either implement lowering or fail with explicit typed unsupported message (no silent fallback).
5) Add/expand smoke coverage so a js-native while-loop program compiles and runs in scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh.

Constraints
- Maintain MIT clean-room approach; behavior-driven implementation only.
- Avoid introducing Dynamic/Any in core logic.
- Keep parser + emitter changes minimal and reviewable.
acceptance_criteria:
- while no longer parses as EUnsupported(while) in native parser statement bodies.
- js-native target compiles and runs a fixture with while loops and correct output.
- npm run -s test:hxhx-targets remains green.
- Any target-specific limitations are explicit and documented (no silent degradation).
notes: Implemented while-statement support end-to-end for current Stage3/js-native path: (1) added SWhile(cond, body, pos) to HxStmt; (2) native parser now parses while (...) body into SWhile instead of EUnsupported(while); (3) typer + macro stmt rewriter + Stage3 unsupported counters recurse through SWhile; (4) js-native statement emitter lowers SWhile to JS while-loops; (5) OCaml Stage3 emitter recursion/dependency walkers and statement lowering now handle SWhile, preserving buildability. Validation: haxe --no-output native parser compile smoke, HXHX_FORCE_STAGE0=1 HXHX_STAGE0_FAILFAST_SECS=1200 bash scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh, and HXHX_BIN=packages/hxhx/out/_build/default/out.bc npm run -s test:hxhx-targets (green).

title: Replace Stage3 backend reflective emit fallback with typed dispatch
description:
Problem
- `packages/hxhx/src/hxhx/Stage3Compiler.hx` still has a reflective fallback in `emitWithBackend`:
  - `Reflect.field(backendReflect, "emit")`
  - `Reflect.callMethod(...)`
- This seam is currently justified as a bootstrap compatibility boundary, but it keeps `Dynamic`/reflection on a correctness-critical path and weakens static guarantees.

Goal
- Remove (or strictly eliminate in default paths) the reflective backend emit fallback by moving to typed backend dispatch contracts for dynamic/bundled providers.

Scope
1) Define typed fallback contract for backend emit dispatch that works in Stage3 bootstrap lane.
2) Replace reflective emit lookup/invoke in `Stage3Compiler.emitWithBackend` with typed dispatch through boundary helpers.
3) Keep compatibility with existing builtin backends and dynamic provider loading semantics.
4) Keep any unavoidable boundary cast isolated in one helper with guardrails.
5) Add/update tests and docs for dispatch policy.

Acceptance criteria
- No `Reflect.callMethod` remains in `Stage3Compiler.emitWithBackend`.
- Builtin target flows (`ocaml-stage3`, `js-native`) remain green.
- Dynamic/bundled provider path still loads and emits successfully in integration tests.
- `ci:guards` + backend wiring/provider tests pass.
- Docs clearly state allowed dispatch boundaries (if any remain).
acceptance_criteria: No Reflect.callMethod in Stage3 emit path; typed dispatch preserved for builtin + dynamic provider backends; tests and guardrails green.
close_reason: Replaced Stage3 emit reflection fallback with typed BackendDispatchBoundary.emit dispatch; added M14 backend dispatch boundary integration tests; added CI guard for Stage3 emit reflection; updated backend layering and builtin backend docs. Validation: test:m14:backend-dispatch-boundary, test:m14:backend-plugin-loader, test:m14:backend-plugin-manifest, test:m14:backend-provider-resolver, test:plugins:strict-matrix, test:hxhx-targets, ci:guards.

title: Bootstrap regen reliability: stage0 binary resolution (native vs wrapper)
description:
During `scripts/hxhx/regenerate-hxhx-bootstrap.sh`, default stage0 resolution (`HAXE_BIN=haxe`) picked `/Users/fullofcaffeine/.nvm/versions/node/v20.19.3/bin/haxe` (Node wrapper), not the native Haxe binary.

Observed in this session:
- Wrapper-backed runs showed prolonged emit stalls with heartbeats up to 700s+ and RSS spikes around 5-7GB.
- Rerun with `HAXE_BIN=/Users/fullofcaffeine/haxe/versions/4.3.7/haxe` showed immediate improvement (early heartbeat RSS ~1.2GB) and materially healthier behavior.

Question to resolve:
- Is wrapper selection expected for bootstrap regen lanes, or should we default to native stage0 Haxe for deterministic resource/latency behavior?

Scope:
1) Reproduce benchmarked comparison (wrapper vs native binary) with report artifacts.
2) Decide bootstrap-stage0 binary selection policy and make default explicit.
3) Implement guardrails (warning/fail-fast/doc guidance) when wrapper binary is detected in critical regen lanes.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Add a documented policy for stage0 binary selection in bootstrap regen (default + override behavior).
2) Add a deterministic check/report in regen flow that logs resolved stage0 binary path and identifies wrapper-vs-native mode.
3) Add regression/perf evidence (at least one reproducible measurement command) proving selected default avoids pathological memory/time behavior.
4) Update docs (`STAGE0_POLICY` and bootstrap/testing docs) with exact commands and troubleshooting guidance.
close_reason: Policy/reporting/benchmark acceptance complete; remaining RSS optimization tracked in child haxe.ocaml-a0pt.1.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa

Additional context from native-plugin happy-path investigation (2026-03-03):

Repro command used:
- HXHX_BOOTSTRAP_HEARTBEAT=20 HXHX_BOOTSTRAP_BUILD_TIMEOUT_SECS=1800 bash scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh

Observed behavior:
- Bootstrap lane progressed normally but had a long tail compiling EmitterStage.ml.
- Peak transient compiler process: ocamlc.opt -impl EmitterStage.ml with RSS around ~2.0GB (sampled via ps), then dropping as compile progressed.
- End-to-end bootstrap build completed in ~220s and produced packages/hxhx/bootstrap_work/_build/default/out.bc.

Interpretation:
- There are likely two separate contributors to memory/runtime pain:
  1) stage0 Haxe wrapper-vs-native binary choice (existing issue scope), and
  2) OCaml bootstrap compile pressure from large generated units (not stage0).

Suggested expansion for this follow-up (or linked child task):
- Capture both dimensions in measurements: stage0 regen memory (wrapper vs native) and bootstrap compile memory (ocamlc.opt on EmitterStage.ml) so root causes are not conflated.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Follow-up variance sweep (2026-03-03): OCAMLRUNPARAM candidate comparison

Method:
- same failfast profile probe for all runs (policy=prefer-native, failfast=65, heartbeat=20, no_opt=0, no_inline=0, disable_prepasses=0)
- 3 runs each for unset, s=2M, s=4M; 1 run for s=8M

Aggregated results (peak_rss_mb):
- unset (n=3): 6172, 6007, 6216
  - avg=6131.67, median=6172
- s=2M (n=3): 4873, 5549, 5299
  - avg=5240.33, median=5299
  - reduction vs unset: avg=14.54%, median=14.14%
- s=4M (n=3): 5012, 4843, 5379
  - avg=5078.00, median=5012
  - reduction vs unset: avg=17.18%, median=18.79%
- s=8M (n=1): 5353
  - reduction vs unset single-sample: avg=12.70%

Interpretation:
- improvement is real but variable; this run family does NOT show stable >=20% reduction on 3-run aggregates.
- among current candidates, s=4M has the strongest aggregate profile; s=2M produced the best single outlier (4873) but weaker aggregate.

Recommendation:
- keep OCAMLRUNPARAM tuning opt-in for now (do not set global default yet).
- next step: longer/full regen comparison for unset vs s=4M to decide whether CI lane default is justified.

title: Bootstrap/source build throughput: native stage0 default + configurable dune workers
description:
Context from 2026-03-04 sessions:
- Running stage0/source lane through the Lix shim (which haxe -> ~/.nvm/.../lix/bin/haxeshim.js) showed severe memory/time behavior (multiple GB spikes; long tail builds).
- Switching to native Haxe binary (/Users/fullofcaffeine/haxe/versions/4.3.7/haxe) immediately improved early heartbeat RSS (roughly from ~7GB windows to ~1.2GB windows in comparable probes) and smoother progress.
- Build path in focus: scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh (source lane with HXHX_FORCE_STAGE0=1) and bootstrap compile via dune.

Problem statement:
Even with native stage0 selection policy work underway, developer UX is still poor for full source rebuilds and CI reruns. We need deterministic, documented throughput controls (especially worker parallelism) and benchmark evidence for safe defaults on local + CI environments.

Scope:
1) Add explicit, documented worker controls for relevant build steps:
   - stage0 Haxe source build lane (where applicable)
   - dune bootstrap build lane (out.bc/out.exe)
2) Benchmark matrix for representative settings:
   - native-vs-wrapper stage0 binary
   - worker counts (e.g., auto, 1, 2, 4, 8)
   - collect wall time + peak RSS from existing heartbeat/report telemetry
3) Choose safe default(s) and expose override knobs in scripts/docs.
4) Ensure CI reproducibility: same knobs available in workflow env with clear marker output.
acceptance_criteria:
1) build-hxhx lane supports deterministic worker configuration via env/flag (documented in scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh help/docs).
2) A benchmark artifact/table is produced for at least one local run and one CI-like run, showing time + peak RSS across worker settings and stage0 binary modes.
3) Selected default setting is justified in docs (STAGE0_POLICY + TESTING + README quick note), including when to override.
4) CI logs include resolved stage0 binary path and effective worker configuration for auditable runs.
5) No behavioral regressions: npm run -s ci:guards passes and gate scripts still execute with default knobs.
close_reason: Implemented worker matrix controls, benchmark artifact table (local + CI-like), docs default/override guidance, and guard validation.

title: Stage0 --connect handoff hang after source emit (client waits while server idle)
description: During source builds with repo server reuse (HXHX_STAGE0_USE_REPO_SERVER=1), the stage0 run can finish generation and populate packages/hxhx/out/**, but the `haxe build.hxml -D ocaml_build=byte --connect <port>` client remains blocked indefinitely. In one run, both client and server dropped to near-idle while the build script kept waiting, requiring manual kill and a direct `dune build ./out.bc` continuation. This creates long false hangs and hides successful progress.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Repro command is deterministic and documented (build-hxhx source lane with --connect). 2) Build script detects stalled or idle --connect handoff and fails fast with actionable message OR auto-recovers by switching to direct non-connect stage0 invocation. 3) On success, script always exits with produced out.bc/out.exe path and no manual kill needed. 4) Add regression coverage (scripted smoke) and doc guidance for when to disable HXHX_STAGE0_USE_REPO_SERVER.
notes: Implemented connect-handoff auto-recovery in scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh: if --connect lane is idle (no log growth + idle process tree) for HXHX_STAGE0_CONNECT_IDLE_SECS, kill stalled client and retry once without --connect. Added deterministic regression smoke scripts/hxhx/test-build-hxhx-connect-retry.sh (npm run test:hxhx:build-connect-retry-smoke), wired into .github/workflows/ci.yml guards job, and documented knob in README.md + docs/01-getting-started/TESTING.md. Local validation: npm run test:hxhx:build-connect-retry-smoke, npm run ci:guards, npm run test:hxhx:cli-contract.
close_reason: Implemented connect stall detector + auto-retry without --connect, added CI smoke coverage, and documented operator knobs.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Second-pass design review for post-stack-sample stage0 memory seam.

Context/evidence:
- `haxe.ocaml-a0pt.1.26` confirmed the current 120s wall is before Reflaxe progress hooks.
- 25s/55s samples are dominated by upstream macro/eval callback execution (`MacroContext`, `MacroApi`, `EvalEmitter`, `EvalEncode`).
- 85s shifts into `MacroApi.encode_type` / `EvalEncode` plus GC pressure.
- Prior A/B evidence rejects broad source-shape splits, `--ocaml-only`, standalone `--no-internal-tools`, standalone `--no-stage3`, `--dce full`, extra callback registration, and cheap graph trims as closure paths.

Rejected options:
- Promote `--no-internal-tools` or `--no-stage3` as default: rejected. The former is non-equivalent as a huge signal and standalone current-head runs regress; the latter standalone also regresses. These cannot support honest Full 1.0 evidence.
- Add or rely on another `Context.onAfterTyping`/macro callback: rejected. The stack evidence and callback-collapse fix show each extra typed callback payload is exactly the expensive surface.
- Try to make Reflaxe avoid typed-module payload entirely in stage0: reject for this slice. That changes target macro architecture and crosses release/provenance semantics; it needs a larger driver/payload design, not a drive-by mitigation.
- Keep doing broad helper/file splits in parser/macro/typer hotspots: rejected. Multiple current-head profiles have already shown regressions or non-durable wins, and the new stack evidence points above those repo-local helper boundaries.

Accepted bounded seam before broad driver split:
- Make the existing `HXHX_STAGE0_NO_DISPLAY` profiling knob real and measurable.
- Rationale:
  - `scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh` already defines and forwards `-D hxhx_stage0_no_display`.
  - There is no matching source guard in `packages/hxhx/src`, and `scripts/hxhx/regenerate-hxhx-bootstrap.sh` / `profile-stage0-regen.sh` do not expose the knob.
  - `DisplayResponseSynthesizer.hx` is 742 lines and Stage3Compiler has display/server integration points. This is a plausible compile-graph trim that is narrower than disabling all Stage3 or all internal tools.
  - If implemented as profiling-only, it does not alter release snapshots or Full 1.0 claims; any evidence must be labelled non-default unless a later parity review promotes it.

Implementation guardrails for the accepted seam:
- Add source guards so `hxhx_stage0_no_display` compiles out display synthesis/request inference only in profiling lanes.
- Add regen/profile pass-through and report fields so A/B evidence is reproducible.
- Validate compile-only with and without `-D hxhx_stage0_no_display`; run guards.
- Profile as an A/B candidate and reject unless it is equivalent-fail-mode and materially improves peak RSS.

Decision:
- Close this xhigh review as a completed second-pass review.
- Open/execute a bounded `thinking:high` child for the no-display profiling trim.
- Do not start broad driver/payload implementation until this narrower existing-dead-knob seam is resolved.

title: Stage0 memory: bootstrap payload strategy spike
description:
Current-head evidence rejects source-shape helper splitting, no-display trimming, no-internal-tools/no-stage3 standalone promotion, DCE, and runtime knobs as stable equivalent mitigations. The remaining credible path is a deliberate driver/payload strategy review and bounded prototype that reduces the pre-Reflaxe macro/eval typed-module payload wall without making non-equivalent release claims.

Acceptance:
1. Record a second-pass design review for the driver/payload seam, including rejected shortcuts and release-equivalence risks.
2. Identify one bounded prototype that can be validated with compile-only checks plus direct stage0 RSS evidence.
3. Implement the bounded prototype only if it preserves release-equivalence or is explicitly profiling-only; record accept/reject evidence and artifact sizes.
close_reason: Xhigh second-pass review complete; no safe quick payload shortcut selected. Filed dedicated stage0-free refresh architecture follow-up.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Second-pass driver/payload strategy review (thinking:xhigh).

Evidence reviewed:
- Multi-sample native stacks show the retained wall inside stage0 macro/eval typed-module encoding: MacroContext/MacroApi/EvalEncode/EvalEmitter, with later GC pressure in encode_type.
- Reflaxe progress/onOutputComplete hooks still do not fire inside the first 120-300s windows, so the wall is before backend output progress.
- Callback-collapse already removed the extra onAfterTyping typed-module callback; the remaining full typed payload is Reflaxe's custom-target/DirectToStringCompiler pass itself.
- Source-shape/helper extraction families are rejected or low-single-digit only: parser, macro scanner/client, ExprMacroExpander, TyperStage.
- Flag/graph trims are rejected as release defaults: no-internal-tools, no-stage3, no-display, no-hx-parser, DCE. The no-stage3+no-internal-tools collapse is real but non-equivalent because it removes the native driver/internal surface from the generated compiler.

Rejected shortcuts:
- Promote no-stage3/no-internal-tools/no-display as committed snapshot defaults: non-equivalent or empirically regressive.
- Add another Context.onAfterTyping/onGenerate side channel: worsens the macro/eval typed payload that is already the sampled wall.
- Keep splitting large Haxe source files blindly: current-head evidence is 0-for-several on the remaining hotspots and often increases RSS.
- Treat ocaml_emit_only or --no-output as payload eliminators: they only skip build/backend output details after the typed graph has already crossed the macro/eval boundary.

Equivalence boundary:
- For release/runtime paths, stage0 source regeneration is already outside the normal path. build-hxhx.sh defaults to committed bootstrap snapshots and release/dist paths enforce HXHX_FORBID_STAGE0=1.
- Therefore the honest release mitigation is to keep normal builds/stage0-forbidden gates on snapshots and treat stage0 source regen as maintainer-only diagnostic work until native/self-hosted refresh exists.
- Full1 perf parity should measure hxhx runtime/native lanes vs upstream haxe, not a maintainer-only stage0 Reflaxe snapshot refresh wall.

Next credible architecture prototype:
- Stage0-free bootstrap refresh or payload slicing, not another Haxe flag:
  1. Native/self-hosted refresh: use built hxhx/Stage3 to regenerate packages/hxhx/bootstrap_out without upstream stage0 haxe.
  2. Monolithic payload slicing: split hxhx bootstrap generation into separately generated/linkable artifacts so no single stage0 Reflaxe invocation has to encode the full Main+Stage3+internal-tools typed graph.
- Both are release-scope architecture work and need their own xhigh design/implementation beads; they are not safe as a quick memory-tuning patch.

Bounded implementation decision for this bead:
- Do not implement a new payload shortcut in this slice. The safe bounded action is to update policy/evidence and move to a dedicated stage0-free refresh/payload-slicing task.
- Immediate local follow-up should also fix bootstrap temp retention, because repeated snapshot builds currently leave large ignored .tmp/hxhx-bootstrap-build.* directories and the user has hit disk pressure.

title: Fix Stage3 full-emit placeholder lowering in MacroState version parser

This closes the immediate bring-up gap for configuration/position helpers but does not close typed reflection/query APIs yet, so bxlg.9.5 remains in progress.

Runtime haxe.macro type plumbing now covers builtin-only Context.getType(), Context.resolveType(), Context.typeof(), Context.toComplexType(), and TypeTools.toString()/toComplexType() for simple builtin/literal cases, with deterministic regression coverage in M14MacroHostRuntimeApiIntegrationTest. The runtime helper deliberately uses a synthetic named-type model rather than claiming full compiler-kind parity. Rich typed reflection/query APIs (for example typeExpr, module/type loading, broader Context/Compiler surfaces) remain open, so bxlg.9.5 stays in progress.

This still does not claim full typed reflection or module loading; getModule(), typeExpr(), richer typed metadata, and broader Context/Compiler surfaces remain open.

This still does not claim typed module metadata or typeExpr parity; richer module loading and typed-expression APIs remain open.

Rich typed reflection and broader typed-expression/module metadata remain open, so bxlg.9.5 stays in_progress.

This does not claim upstream package-recursive include semantics, ignore filters, explicit classPaths, or strict mode; those remain open under bxlg.9.5.

Covered by test:m14:macro-host-runtime-api plus macro-runtime-mode-switch. Important limitation: runtime unify currently stays deliberately narrow (equality + Dynamic wildcard + Null<T>/T) because broader haxe.macro.Type constructor matching still trips current OCaml codegen around TAbstract/module-type constructor collisions; richer typed reflection remains open under bxlg.9.5.

This is intentionally a seeded snapshot capability, not live typer callsite parity, but it closes the previous missing Context.getCallArguments() surface and adds end-to-end regression coverage.

Integration coverage now asserts generated module source for imports/usings plus multiple emitted types. This is intentionally a small compatibility slice, not upstream-equivalent typed module mutation; richer defineModule semantics and typed module metadata remain open.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: 2026-03-07 xhigh follow-up: reviewed remaining runtime macro gaps against actual repo call sites. The next materially missing seam is not another Context getter; it is richer runtime Type fidelity. In particular, runtime TypeTools.applyTypeParameters() is still identity-only and TypeTools.iter() is still effectively a no-op for the synthetic external-host model, while real reflaxe.ocaml compiler code uses applyTypeParameters() heavily on TType/TAbstract paths. Closing bxlg.9.5 before either (a) widening the runtime Type model enough to make those semantics honest, or (b) explicitly scoping them out of Full1, would be misleading. Recommendation: stop adding convenience rungs and treat the next step as either a deliberate richer-Type-model slice or a scope decision under bxlg.9.6/f1cl.4.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: 2026-03-07: landed the next honest runtime Type fidelity slice. External-host runtime TypeTools.applyTypeParameters() now performs recursive substitution through the current synthetic Type model, TypeTools.iter() now traverses direct children instead of no-oping, and follow(TType(...)) now substitutes typedef payload params. Validation is through the external-host macro probe rather than direct Type pattern-matching, because generated OCaml still cannot safely reconstruct or destructure synthetic TAbstract wrappers without hitting the upstream constructor-name collision in haxe.macro.Type / ModuleType. Remaining fidelity gap is therefore narrower and explicit: synthetic abstract-wrapper preservation and richer typed/module metadata are still below Full1 expectations.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: 2026-03-07 xhigh sufficiency review: still not closable. The latest runtime Type slice removes the worst lie (applyTypeParameters is no longer identity-only, iter is no longer a no-op, and follow(TType(...)) now substitutes typedef payload params), which is enough for the current reflaxe.ocaml typedef-heavy call sites and the external-host probe. But it is still below an honest Full1 macro API parity claim. Two semantic seams remain material: (1) synthetic abstract-wrapper fidelity is still missing, so followWithAbstracts/applyTypeParameters over abstract-heavy paths still collapse to underlying types instead of preserving a real abstract wrapper; (2) synthetic module/type metadata is still narrower than upstream because enum/typedef/abstract declaration kinds still round-trip as class-shaped refs in external-host mode. This matters beyond synthetic probes: vendored reflaxe.elixir code exercises applyTypeParameters + followWithAbstracts over typedef/abstract-rich flows. Recommendation: do not move to bxlg.9.6 yet. The next acceptable step is a deliberate xhigh slice for synthetic abstract-wrapper fidelity and richer declaration-kind/module metadata, or an explicit Full1 scope decision that those semantics are out of scope.

title: js-native: support break/continue loop control markers
description:
Problem
- Native parser currently represents `break;` and `continue;` as `SExpr(EUnsupported("break"|"continue"), ...)`.
- js-native emit currently treats all `EUnsupported(...)` as hard errors, so loop-control statements fail even in simple loop code.

Scope
1) Add explicit js-native lowering for statement-level `EUnsupported("break")` and `EUnsupported("continue")`.
2) Keep behavior narrow: only statement positions should lower to JS loop-control keywords.
3) Do not broaden unsupported-expression semantics globally; preserve fail-fast behavior for other unsupported expression kinds.
4) Add target smoke coverage for break/continue in loop bodies.

Constraints
- Keep non-js backends unchanged.
- No `Any`; avoid new `Dynamic` usage.
- Keep implementation small and easy to remove once parser gains structured `SBreak`/`SContinue` nodes.
acceptance_criteria:
- js-native can emit+run a fixture using `break` and `continue` inside loops.
- Existing js-native and Stage3 target tests remain green.
- Unsupported expression handling still fails fast for non-whitelisted raw markers.
notes:
Implemented narrow js-native lowering for loop-control markers emitted by native parser:
- `JsStmtEmitter` now maps `SExpr(EUnsupported("break"), ...)` to `break;`
- `JsStmtEmitter` now maps `SExpr(EUnsupported("continue"), ...)` to `continue;`
- other unsupported expression kinds remain fail-fast.

Added smoke fixture `JsNativeLoopControlMain` to `scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh` validating while+break+continue output (`js-native-loop-control:5:8`).

Validation:
- `haxe -cp packages/hxhx/src -cp packages/hih-compiler/src -cp packages/reflaxe.ocaml/src -cp packages/reflaxe.ocaml/std -main hxhx.Main --no-output -D hih_native_parser`

- `HXHX_BIN=packages/hxhx/out/_build/default/out.bc npm run -s test:hxhx-targets`
All green.

title: hih AST: make break/continue first-class statements
description:
Problem
- Native parser currently lowers `break;` and `continue;` as `SExpr(EUnsupported("break"|"continue"), ...)`.
- js-native currently has a marker-specific workaround in statement emission.
- This keeps loop control out of the typed statement model and makes semantics indirect.

Goal
- Promote loop control to first-class statement nodes in the Stage3 AST.
- Keep js-native semantics explicit and remove dependency on unsupported-expression markers for normal control flow.

Scope
1) Add statement nodes for break/continue in `HxStmt`.
2) Parse `break` and `continue` into those nodes in native parser.
3) Update typer traversal / macro stmt rewriting / unsupported counters for new nodes.
4) Update js-native stmt emitter to lower new nodes directly.
5) Update OCaml Stage3 stmt handling to compile safely with the new nodes (no pattern-match gaps).
6) Remove now-redundant js-native marker special-casing for break/continue.

Constraints
- Keep this change narrow and behavior-preserving for existing tests.
- Do not use `Any`; avoid new `Dynamic` unless strictly boundary-related.
- Preserve fail-fast for truly unsupported expression forms.
acceptance_criteria:
- Native parser no longer emits `EUnsupported("break")` / `EUnsupported("continue")` for statement-level loop control.
- js-native loop-control smoke still passes.
- Full `npm run -s test:hxhx-targets` passes.
- No remaining js-native statement-emitter dependence on unsupported break/continue markers.
notes:
Implemented first-class statement nodes for loop control in the HIH AST.

Changes
- Added `SBreak(pos)` and `SContinue(pos)` to `HxStmt`.
- Native parser now lowers `break;` / `continue;` to these nodes (instead of `SExpr(EUnsupported(...))`).
- Updated statement traversal sites:
  - typer (`TyperStage`)
  - macro statement rewriter (`ExprMacroExpander`)
  - Stage3 unsupported counters (`Stage3Compiler`)
  - function return scanning (`HxFunctionDecl`)
- js-native emitter now lowers `SBreak`/`SContinue` directly and no longer depends on unsupported-marker pattern matching.
- OCaml Stage3 emitter now handles `SBreak`/`SContinue` in statement lowering and dependency-walk switches so builds remain total.

Validation
- `haxe -cp packages/hxhx/src -cp packages/hih-compiler/src -cp packages/reflaxe.ocaml/src -cp packages/reflaxe.ocaml/std -main hxhx.Main --no-output -D hih_native_parser`
- `HXHX_FORCE_STAGE0=1 HXHX_STAGE0_FAILFAST_SECS=3600 bash scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh`
- `HXHX_BIN=packages/hxhx/out/_build/default/out.bc npm run -s test:hxhx-targets`
All green; js-native loop-control and do/while smoke lanes pass.
close_reason: break/continue promoted to first-class statements and validated across Stage3/js-native flows.

title: backend boundary follow-up: centralize GenIrProgram recovery cast helper
description:
Context
- We currently use `requireProgram(program:GenIrProgram):GenIrProgram { return cast program; }` in:
  - `packages/hih-compiler/src/backend/js/JsTargetCore.hx`
  - `packages/hih-compiler/src/backend/ocaml/OcamlTargetCore.hx`
- This cast is currently justified because reflaxe/OCaml dispatch can degrade `ITargetCore.emit` parameters to `Obj.t` at generated OCaml interface boundaries.
- Without boundary recovery, Stage0 build fails in generated ML with type mismatch:
  - `program has type Obj.t but expected MacroExpandedProgram.t`.

Problem
- The cast is correct today, but duplicated in multiple target cores.
- Duplicated boundary recovery logic increases drift risk and obscures where dynamic recovery is allowed.
- We need one canonical, documented boundary policy that survives backend growth (js/ocaml and future promoted targets).

Goal
- Centralize `GenIrProgram` boundary recovery in one shared helper/pattern.
- Keep target-core emitters fully typed and free of ad-hoc boundary casts.
- Preserve current behavior and Stage0 build stability.

Scope
1) Design a shared helper for boundary recovery (single location, minimal surface).
2) Migrate `JsTargetCore` and `OcamlTargetCore` to the shared helper.
3) Define explicit policy for where boundary casts are allowed vs forbidden.
4) Add a targeted regression check that would fail if boundary recovery is removed or drifted.
5) Document the final pattern in backend architecture docs.

Proposed Implementation (candidate)
- Add one utility under backend layer, e.g. `packages/hih-compiler/src/backend/GenIrBoundary.hx`:
  - `public static inline function requireProgram(program:GenIrProgram):GenIrProgram`.
- Replace local `requireProgram(...)` duplicates in target cores with helper call.
- Keep any unavoidable casts at Stage3 reflection/provider seams explicitly documented.

Constraints
- No upstream code copying; keep MIT clean-room workflow.
- No behavior change in backend output.
- Keep changes minimal and reviewable.

Risk/Tradeoffs
- Over-aggressive refactor could destabilize Stage3 bootstrap.
- Keeping duplicates invites divergence when additional target cores land.

Validation
- `haxe -cp packages/hxhx/src -cp packages/hih-compiler/src -cp packages/reflaxe.ocaml/src -cp packages/reflaxe.ocaml/std -main hxhx.Main --no-output -D hih_native_parser`
- `npm run -s test:hxhx:builtin-target-smoke`
- If available in same session: a Stage0 bootstrap build proving no `Obj.t` vs `MacroExpandedProgram.t` regression in generated ML.

Notes
- This is follow-up technical debt after boundary hardening work in `haxe.ocaml-3b7`.
- Priority intentionally set to later (not blocker) because current casts are correct and localized.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A shared backend boundary helper exists and is used by both JsTargetCore and OcamlTargetCore instead of duplicated local requireProgram helpers. 2) Cast policy is documented: allowed only at explicit boundary seams; forbidden in core emitter logic. 3) Compile + smoke validation pass (native parser no-output + builtin target smoke). 4) At least one bootstrap/generated-ML validation note is recorded showing no Obj.t vs MacroExpandedProgram.t regression.
notes: Implemented central boundary helper packages/hih-compiler/src/backend/GenIrBoundary.hx and migrated JsTargetCore/OcamlTargetCore to it. Added explicit Stage3 backend-dispatch seam handling so reflaxe OCaml output no longer regresses Obj.t vs MacroExpandedProgram at the emit bridge boundary (validated with HXHX_FORCE_STAGE0=1 HXHX_STAGE0_FAILFAST_SECS=1200 bash scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh). Also validated native parser compile smoke and full target workflow (HXHX_BIN=packages/hxhx/out/_build/default/out.bc npm run -s test:hxhx-targets).

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Implemented local fix for Full1 `--each` / `--next` planning failures.

Root cause:
- Top-level CLI routing used the Stage1 single-unit HXML expansion path for target planning.
- That path rejects multi-unit directives, prints `unsupported hxml directive: --each/--next`, and leaves top-level routing with unexpanded args, which can degrade to `No target selected`.

Change:
- `CliRouting.planningTargetArgs()` now uses the existing multi-unit `Hxml.expandArgsToUnits()` parser and flattens units only for target-scan planning.
- Actual forwarded args remain unchanged, so Stage3 still owns real per-unit execution.
- Updated Hxml docs to reflect current multi-unit support.
- Added a CLI contract regression for multi-unit non-JS HXML classification and multi-unit JS HXML native routing.
- Regenerated `packages/hxhx/bootstrap_out/hxhx_CliRouting.ml`.

Local evidence:
- `npm run test:m14:direct-flag-cli-contract` PASS.
- `npm run ci:guards` PASS.
- `git diff --check` PASS.
- `HAXE_BIN="$(command -v haxe)" bash scripts/hxhx/regenerate-hxhx-bootstrap.sh --fast --stage0-no-line-directives` PASS in 43s.
- `HXHX_FORCE_STAGE0=0 bash scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh` PASS.
- Bootstrap-built no-stage0 probe:
  - non-JS multi-unit HXML with `--each` / `--next` now exits with `Target not supported natively; rerun with --compat.`
  - it no longer emits `unsupported hxml directive` or `No target selected`.
  - JS multi-unit HXML with `--each` / `--next` produces two `stage3=no_emit_ok` units.

Artifact hygiene:
- Removed bootstrap build/probe directories.
- Ran `npm run clean:tmp` and `npm run clean`.
- Final transient footprint: `.tmp` about 1.4M, `.artifacts` 0B.

Pending:
- Push and inspect Full1 strict remote evidence. The expected effect is that Python/Java/Cs move from HXML directive/no-target failures to the honest native target support gap.

title: Full1 extended targets: close native target/toolchain gaps
description: Full1 strict matrix still fails non-JS extended targets honestly: Neko/Hl/Cpp report unsupported native target and Lua is missing from PATH. Decide and implement the native target/toolchain path required for the release claim, without weakening strict no-skip evidence.
design: Second-pass design review (xhigh): Current evidence shows Full1 extended target runner/toolchain plumbing is honest: Macro/JS have native paths, and Neko/Hl/Python/Java/Cs/Cpp/Lua/Php all reach target compile then fail at hxhx native target selection. The remaining blocker is architectural, not CI: strict non-delegating Full1 equivalence requires native implementations or plugin-backed implementations for each standard Haxe target generator, plus runtime/toolchain integration evidence. Weakening FULL1_GATE3_EXTENDED_TARGETS or removing these targets would be a public release-scope change and must not be done as a bug fix. Compatibility fallback via --compat is explicitly disallowed under HXHX_FORBID_STAGE0=1 and cannot satisfy this gate. Recommended path: keep the strict extended gate failing honestly; split implementation tracks by target backend family (Neko/HL bytecode, source targets Python/Java/Cs/Php/Lua/Cpp) or record an explicit product-scope decision that Full 1.0 is not the current release claim while Scoped 1.0 remains the ship claim. Closure criterion for this bead remains unchanged: either native target support lands and gate evidence passes, or a reviewed release-scope change is made in the contract docs/manifest with guard updates.
acceptance_criteria: Full1 strict matrix either passes the declared native extended targets with per-target artifacts or has an xhigh-reviewed scope change recorded before public 1.0 claims; no target is silently skipped under strict mode.
notes: Remote evidence after bb7ceaec: workflow_dispatch run 24589922639 with targets=Neko,Hl,Cpp reached each target compile. Neko installed utest and failed at compile-neko.hxml with 'Target not supported natively.' Hl built/validated HashLink 1.16.0, registered the hashlink haxelib path, then failed at compile-hl.hxml with the same native unsupported diagnostic. Cpp installed hxcpp and failed while compiling hxcpp tools with hxhx on the same native unsupported diagnostic. Summary: Neko FAIL (2s), Hl FAIL (9s), Cpp FAIL (4s). Combined current classification: all extended non-JS targets now pass runner/toolchain preflight and fail honestly on native target support/scope, not silent skips or missing tools.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Implemented a focused behavior-driven fix for the strict Gate3 JS TestHttp parse EOF regression.

Root cause: HxConditionalCompilation recognized line-start block directives but did not treat `#end;` as a directive terminator with an expression semicolon suffix. In a TestHttp-shaped static final initializer with a same-line inline guard followed by a block conditional, filtering left a literal `#end;` in the active source, which then reached the Stage3 parser.

Change:
- Added a clean-room regression in `test/M14ConditionalCompilationIntegrationTest.hx` covering static final initializer + inline same-line guard + nested block conditional + `#end;` suffix + expression-bodied lambda method.
- Updated `HxConditionalCompilation.filterSource` to recognize `#end;`, blank the directive token, and preserve the semicolon as surrounding Haxe expression syntax.
- Regenerated the committed `packages/hxhx/bootstrap_out/HxConditionalCompilation.ml` snapshot; unrelated generator churn was intentionally reversed so this slice stays focused.

Evidence:
- Pre-fix regression failed with surviving `#end` as expected.
- `npm run test:m14:conditional-compilation` PASS.
- Direct temporary oracle-file probe against upstream Haxe 4.3.7 `tests/unit/src/unit/TestHttp.hx` PASS: filtered source parsed without EOF (`ok classes=1 fields=1`). The upstream file/probe stayed in `.tmp` and was removed before commit.
- Bootstrap snapshot build PASS: `HXHX_BOOTSTRAP_BUILD_DIR=.tmp/testhttp-filter-build HXHX_FORCE_STAGE0=0 bash scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh` produced `out.bc`.
- Focused Gate3 JS local evidence: `bash scripts/hxhx/run-upstream-runci-targets.sh Js` advanced past the previous `compile-js.hxml` / `TestHttp.hx` parse failure and completed many upstream JS unit variants with `10983/10983` assertions passing. It later failed in upstream server/retyper tests on macOS; that is downstream of this parser regression and remains covered by the broader Full1 extended-target work until Linux CI confirms current status.
- `npm run ci:guards` PASS.
- `HXHX_BIN=.tmp/testhttp-filter-build/_build/default/out.bc HXHX_FORCE_STAGE0=0 npm run test:hxhx-targets` PASS (`OK: hxhx lanes`, elapsed 590s).

Docs/Goals review:
- README Goals status table reviewed. No update required: this is an internal parser/filter correctness fix and does not change public workflows, flags, tooling, or production-readiness status by itself. The Full1 JS evidence improves from early TestHttp parse failure to a later suite tail, but public readiness remains governed by the strict Gate3/Full1 gates.

Artifact hygiene:
- Ran `npm run clean:tmp`, `npm run clean`, removed temporary upstream oracle/probe/build scratch paths, then ran `npm run clean:deep` after repeated bootstrap regeneration. Disk-heavy transient output was cleaned; `.tmp` is back to small historical fixture residue (~31M). Untracked `repomix-output.txt` was left untouched.

title: Gate3 Full1 all-target workflow: avoid 3h timeout after Lua reaches fourth VM
description: Current-head all-target Gate3 Full1 Extended Strict workflow can exceed the GitHub job timeout even after focused target lanes pass. Run 27399425138 on d304ff65902f89e1b050d521bcc78898132f33ea was cancelled at the 3h job limit while executing Lua sys compile for the fourth Lua VM variant. Earlier Lua variants had already passed unit/sys/misc phases, and the inner timing artifact misleadingly marked strict_extended_gate3_matrix as pass because cancellation happened at the job boundary before the aggregate marker could be emitted. This task owns remote workflow throughput/sharding/caching so all requested targets can publish a trustworthy strict aggregate result without weakening semantics.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Gate3 Full1 all-target strict workflow completes within GitHub timeout on current source, or is safely sharded into aggregate jobs with the same strict no-skip semantics. 2) The final evidence emits/preserves FULL1_GATE3_EXTENDED_TARGETS:PASS only when all requested targets actually complete and pass. 3) Timing/artifact summaries distinguish job cancellation from true matrix pass. 4) Bead haxe.ocaml-f1cl.3.1 is updated with the resulting current-head all-target evidence. 5) Docs/README Goals table review is recorded; update docs only if workflow usage, release contract, or production-readiness status changes.

- repo root: `vendor/reflaxe-elixir`

4. Any remaining gaps are turned into narrower follow-up beads.

title: Define native source-host adapter contract for Reflaxe-style custom-target HXML workflows
description: The pybm verifier now proves that ordinary source-based reflaxe.elixir HXML workflows (for example compile.hxml/build-tests.hxml using -D elixir_output plus CompilerInit.Start()) do not currently map onto any native hxhx host lane. This is broader than a simple CLI parse bug: Stage3 currently supports builtin JS/OCaml lanes and explicit backend provider/plugin activation, but no generic source-host adapter contract for Reflaxe-style custom targets. We need an explicit design decision for whether and how hxhx should support these workflows natively.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A written contract explains whether source-based Reflaxe target HXML workflows are in scope for native hxhx-as-haxe support, with concrete trigger signals and routing rules. 2. The chosen path is explicit: either (a) implement a minimal native host-adapter surface for one real workflow such as reflaxe.elixir compile.hxml, or (b) document that pybm must use a different native artifact/host path and update verifier/docs accordingly. 3. The outcome is recorded in bead comments/docs with artifact references from pybm, not left as an implicit assumption.
close_reason: Closed after explicit written second-pass design review. The repo contract now recommends explicit host-adapter/plugin lanes as the official native verification path for external Reflaxe workloads, keeps raw source-based HXML invocations as diagnostic baseline evidence, updates docs to match, and creates follow-up bead haxe.ocaml-k6rz to enforce that contract in the verifier.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Initial design note (2026-03-18): local evidence narrows this to three real paths, not one. (A) Add a native source-host adapter lane in hxhx itself: detect a source-based Reflaxe custom-target workflow (for example elixir_output + CompilerInit.Start or similar explicit markers) and route it into Stage3 with a declared backend/provider contract. This would make hxhx act as a true haxe replacement for these workflows, but it expands CLI/compiler scope and needs a crisp contract for how source libraries expose provider metadata. (B) Keep core hxhx strict and require explicit host adapters/plugin manifests for native use, then update pybm to verify the native artifact through that adapter path instead of raw haxe compile.hxml compatibility. This matches existing docs/02-user-guide/HXHX_PROMOTION_HOST_ADAPTERS.md and the proven promotion lanes. (C) Explicitly declare raw source-based Reflaxe-target HXML workflows out of scope for native host replacement and keep pybm as a diagnostic-only baseline comparison tool. Current repo state favors B or C more than A: Stage3 already supports builtin JS/OCaml plus explicit provider/plugin activation, but there is no generic source-host adapter surface and no native Elixir backend provider in vendor/reflaxe-elixir to auto-discover.

  - no source-host discovery contract exists for `-D elixir_output=...` + `CompilerInit.Start()` style workflows
- Promotion doctrine: `docs/02-user-guide/HXHX_PROMOTION_HOST_ADAPTERS.md` and `docs/00-project/REFLAXE_PROMOTION_MATRIX_CONTRACT.md`
  - current native promotion contract is adapter/plugin based
  - supported official paths are builtin target and explicit plugin path, not implicit raw-source custom-target discovery
- Pressure-test workflow shape:
  - `vendor/reflaxe-elixir/test/snapshot/core/try_catch/compile.hxml` uses `-D elixir_output=out` plus `--macro reflaxe.elixir.CompilerInit.Start()`
  - `vendor/reflaxe-elixir/examples/todo-app/build-tests.hxml` uses `-D elixir_output=test/generated` and `-lib reflaxe.elixir`
  - neither declares an `hxhx_backend_plugin_manifest` or `hxhx_backend_provider`

Option review
- A) Add native source-host adapter discovery to `hxhx` itself
  - upside: strongest `hxhx as haxe replacement` story for Reflaxe custom targets
  - cost: new CLI/compiler contract, backend metadata discovery design, likely broader scope than current promotion matrix, and risk of inventing semantics that upstream Haxe does not define as a native `hxhx` concern
  - current repo evidence does not yet justify this as the default path
- B) Keep official native support on explicit host-adapter/plugin lanes and make `pybm` verify that declared path
  - upside: matches current promotion docs, current Stage3 ABI, and already-proven `RPMX_HXHX_PLUGIN:PASS` lane
  - keeps native support honest and measurable
  - lets raw source-based HXML workflows remain a diagnostic comparison instead of an implied support contract
- C) Explicitly declare raw source-based Reflaxe-target HXML workflows out of scope for native `hxhx-as-haxe`
  - upside: cleanest boundary
  - cost: too negative alone; it would leave `pybm` without an official native verification path unless paired with B

Recommendation
- Choose B as the official path, with C only as the diagnostic boundary statement for raw source-host invocations.
- Concretely: native support for external Reflaxe targets should be measured through declared promotion host adapters/plugins, not by assuming `hxhx` already auto-discovers arbitrary source-based custom-target HXML workflows.
- Raw source-based `reflaxe.elixir` invocations should remain useful baseline diagnostics, but they should not be treated as required native compatibility proofs unless we later explicitly widen scope and implement A.

Implications for existing beads
- `haxe.ocaml-pybm.1` should no longer be treated as an unconditional must-fix compatibility bug. Under the recommended contract, it is either:
  - superseded by adapter-path verification work, or
  - retained only as a diagnostic gap bead if we want to track a future scope expansion toward A.
- The next implementation bead should adapt the verifier/docs so the official native lane is the promoted adapter/plugin path and the raw source-based lane is labeled diagnostic/baseline.

Acceptance boundary for closing this bead
- This bead can close once the repo docs and pybm tracking explicitly adopt the recommendation above and the next implementation bead exists to enforce it in verifier output.

title: Define self-promotion contract for reflaxe.ocaml as a native hxhx target surface
description:
Track the explicit self-promotion goal for reflaxe.ocaml itself. The repo should distinguish source-level `-lib reflaxe.ocaml` usage from a promoted native hxhx target-surface usage, and decide the first-class supported shape for reflaxe.ocaml under hxhx (builtin, plugin, or staged path).

Scope:
- define what it means for reflaxe.ocaml to promote itself as a native target surface
- decide whether the first-class supported surface is builtin, plugin, or a staged recommendation
- prove at least one official native hxhx workflow that uses reflaxe.ocaml through that promoted surface rather than only through source-level library loading
- document how this fits with the existing promotion matrix and with standalone upstream `haxe + reflaxe.ocaml` usage

Acceptance criteria:
1. A documented contract exists for reflaxe.ocaml self-promotion as a native hxhx target surface.
2. At least one promoted native hxhx workflow for reflaxe.ocaml is proven with runnable artifacts.
3. Docs clearly separate source-level `-lib reflaxe.ocaml` use from promoted target-surface use.
4. Any deferred path (builtin or plugin) is explicitly called out with rationale.
close_reason: Oracle-guided contract closure landed. Docs now explicitly separate reflaxe.ocaml source-level upstream usage from official native hxhx builtin and plugin surfaces, with matrix evidence already proving those promoted paths.

title: Codegen: support ++/-- on instance fields
description:
We currently drop OpIncrement/OpDecrement when the operand is not a ref-local (e.g. `self.i++`), which can cause infinite loops in generated OCaml (e.g. lexers).

Implement `++/--` lowering for:
- instance var fields (`TField(_, FInstance(...))`)
- static vars
- array elements (`TArray`) where feasible

Prefer correct statement semantics first; document expression-value nuances (prefix/postfix) for later.
acceptance_criteria:
- `self.i++` and `self.i--` update record fields in generated OCaml
- Add a regression test that would otherwise hang (e.g. lexer/index increment)
- Ensure generated code remains `-warn-error` clean

title: hih native frontend: extend protocol to carry statement bodies
description: Protocol v1 only transmits method summaries (signature + first-return hints), which prevents Stage3 from emitting full OCaml bodies when using the native frontend.\n\nWe currently work around this for bring-up via HIH_FORCE_HX_PARSER=1 (pure-Haxe parser) when --hxhx-emit-full-bodies is enabled, but that won't scale to upstream modules that the pure parser cannot yet parse.
design: Add a backward-compatible protocol extension (prefer bumping to v=2) that can transmit a minimal statement AST for function bodies. Keep the subset aligned with HxStmt/HxExpr (SBlock/SVar/SIf/SExpr/SReturn/SReturnVoid + basic Expr forms like call/field/binop/unop/literals/ident).\n\nDecoding should be best-effort: unknown stmt/expr forms map to EUnsupported so the pipeline can keep progressing.
acceptance_criteria: - Native parser can emit bodies for the minimal subset (at least SExpr(trace("HELLO");)).\n- ParserStage decoder rehydrates bodies into HxFunctionDecl.body.\n- Stage3 --hxhx-emit-full-bodies no longer needs HIH_FORCE_HX_PARSER for the subset (add a regression test).
close_reason: Implemented

title: Modular hxhx customization and Haxe-family variation architecture
description: Define and eventually implement the architecture for bending hxhx/Haxe without corrupting the baseline Haxe 4.3.7 compatibility contract. This owns two related goals from docs/00-project/NORTH_STAR_GOALS.md: pluggable compiler customization and deliberate Haxe-family compiler variations/forks in Haxe. The baseline hxhx release must remain Haxe-compatible by default; custom behavior must be explicit, removable, documented, and CI-auditable.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A design doc defines supported extension points for compiler customization versus full compiler variations/dialects. 2) The model keeps baseline hxhx Haxe 4.3.7 compatibility as the default and prevents plugins/variations from silently weakening parity claims. 3) At least one minimal pluggable customization proof exists with enable/disable behavior and deterministic tests. 4) At least one documented variation/fork workflow exists for creating a deliberate Haxe-family compiler product in Haxe. 5) README Goals status and docs/00-project/NORTH_STAR_GOALS.md are updated when production-readiness changes.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Scope clarification: this track is not only about plugins. A core reason for hxhx is to make Haxe itself easier to hack because the compiler is implemented in Haxe. Design work should therefore cover compiler readability, modular seams, behavior-driven tests for safe edits, and deliberate fork/variation workflows, while keeping baseline hxhx Haxe 4.3.7-compatible by default.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Second-pass design review for xhigh scope: the KPI patch removes eager startup registration of generated Type metadata and installs HxTypeRegistry.init as a lazy HxType hook before main. This preserves reflection semantics because Type.resolveClass/resolveEnum, Type.get*Fields, Type.createInstance/createEnum, enumConstructor, typed-catch tag lookup, and Std.isOfType now force the hook before reading registry tables. Registration helpers intentionally do not force initialization, because HxTypeRegistry.init is implemented in terms of those helpers; setting registry_initialized before invoking the hook avoids reentrant initialization. This is a performance-only implementation change, not a scope/policy exception. Local evidence before remote KPI rerun: stage0-free no-emit smoke passed stage3=no_emit_ok with resolved_modules=1; PORTABLE_FIXTURE_ALLOWLIST=type_reflection_basic,typed_catches,typed_catches_dynamic bash scripts/test-portable.sh passed; npm run test:snapshot passed; npm run ci:guards and git diff --check passed. title: M16 — Haxe-in-Haxe compiler (Haxe 4.3.7 + macros)
description:
Track the path to a production-ready Haxe-in-Haxe compiler example under `examples/`.

- Use the OCaml Haxe compiler source as reference: /Users/fullofcaffeine/workspace/code/haxe.elixir.reference/haxe

2026-02-11: Implemented native-frontend parser/lexer fixes for upstream std parsing gaps.

Landed
- packages/reflaxe.ocaml/std/runtime/HxHxNativeLexer.ml: add regex literal tokenization for ~/.../flags (prevents quote chars inside regex from breaking lexing).
- packages/reflaxe.ocaml/std/runtime/HxHxNativeParser.ml: accept regex token kind and allow keyword-named function identifier 'as' in declaration position (cs.Lib compatibility).
- packages/hih-compiler/src/HxConditionalCompilation.hx: strip // comment tails before directive '#'-heuristic so lines like '#if cs // issue #996' still participate in the conditional stack.
- scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh: added regressions for regex-with-quote literals, keyword-named function declarations, and '#if ... // #...' directive parsing.
- docs/02-user-guide/HXHX_NATIVE_FRONTEND_PROTOCOL.md: documented regex token kind.

Validation
- npm run -s test:hxhx-targets -> green
- npm run -s test:upstream:runci-macro-stage3-display -> green
- npm run -s test:upstream:runci-macro -> gate2_stage3_no_emit_direct=ok
- npm run -s ci:guards -> green

Gate1 status after this fix
- npm run -s test:upstream:unit-macro now advances past previous parse_failed blockers and fails later at Unit_TestXML Xml.createElement (tracked separately in haxe.ocaml-xgv.10.14).

title: Gate1 stage3 emit: fix Php_Boot unary INF float typing
description: Gate1 native stage3 emit now fails in generated Php_Boot.ml at expression `(-(Php_Const.iNF))` with OCaml type error (int vs float). We need deterministic float-safe lowering/post-processing for this upstream php boot shape.
acceptance_criteria: - npm run -s test:upstream:unit-macro no longer fails at Php_Boot unary INF type mismatch\n- Add/keep Stage3 regression coverage for unary minus over php.Const.INF shape\n- Keep npm run -s test:hxhx-targets and npm run -s ci:guards green

title: Chore: reduce hih-compiler workload acceptance runtime
description: The workloads/hih-compiler compile is CPU-heavy and can run for several minutes in local acceptance runs, which slows iteration and can look hung.
acceptance_criteria:
- Establish baseline runtime in CI/local for workloads/hih-compiler
- Add explicit runtime budget + timeout/heartbeat guidance in docs

- Keep full heavy workload runnable in dedicated gate path
